learning_outcomes.text: Acquire the methodological knowledge necessary to understand the operation and derive input/output relations of resistive and dynamic electrical networks, also in the presence of active components.
Develop the ability to appropriately use the terminology of the discipline in order to understand the literature related to the operation of electrical networks.
Develop the ability to appropriately use the terminology of the discipline in order to effectively present topics inherent to the discipline.
Develop the ability to appropriately use the terminology of the discipline in order to critically discuss topics covered during the course.
Develop the necessary competencies to continue studies and autonomously provide for one's own updating.
Understand techniques, methods and their limits, being aware of the non-technical implications of engineering practice.

Develop the ability to combine theory and practice to solve multidisciplinary engineering problems, taking into account constraints also of a non-technical nature, and operating in collaboration with other engineers or other professionals typically present in manufacturing companies.
Knowledge of the principles of industrial electrotechnics, electrical machines, industrial robotics and controls used in industrial plants.

Ability to solve problems related to resistive and dynamic electrical networks, also in the presence of active components, to choose and use electrical machines within mechanical systems, analyzing their performance, to design automatic feedback control systems, also with the aid of computer tools, to understand the operation of manipulators and mobile robots most used in industrial and non-industrial applications, to choose appropriate actuators (electric, hydraulic and pneumatic) for machines and plants.
Technical communication in written form (preparation of individual reports and relations).
Development of adequate technical expression and discussion of one's arguments.

syllabus_topics: Analysis of circuits in RPC (Resistive-Capacitive-Inductive Circuits)
Generalization of methods and systematic writing
Analysis of circuits in RPS (Sinusoidal Steady State)
Application to circuits of arbitrary order
Circuit simulation in MATLAB and CAD environment
Simulation of circuits in CAD/CAE environments based on SPICE language
Circuit theory and its applicability limits
Analysis of circuits in the time domain
Calculation of steady-state response with constant excitations
Equivalent circuits in the phasor domain
Active power, power factor, reactive power, apparent power and complex power
Analysis of symmetric and balanced three-phase systems
Three-phase systems with and without neutral wire
teaching_methods: Classroom explanations of theoretical concepts with application examples
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a preliminary written test followed by an oral test. Midterm tests can replace the written exam for the current academic year if passed with a score of at least 18 (or one at least 18 and another not less than 14). Students can choose to retake the full written exam, but this choice forfeits any previous midterm scores. Both written and oral exams cover the entire program. A minimum score of 18 is required for each test to be considered passed.
